=== RRR--Response to Oncor LCRA Objection to Supp Direct 05-29-26.docx ===
SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349
PUC DOCKET NO. 59475

JOINT APPLICATION OF ONCOR	§	BEFORE THE STATE OFFICE
ELECTRIC DELIVERY COMPANY	§
LLC ANF LSRA TSC TO AMEND		§			
THEIR CERTIFICATES OF		§
CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY	§	
FOR THE BELL COUNTY EAST		§
SWITCH TO BIG HILL SUBSTATION	§			OF
765-KV TRANSMISSION LINE IN	§
BELL, BURNET, CONCHO,		§
CORYELL, LAMPASSAS, LLANO,	§
MASON, MCCULLOCH, MENARD,	§
MILAM, MILES, SAN SABA,		§
SCHLEICHER, TOM GREEN, AND	§
WILLIAMSON COUNTIES		§	ADMINISTRATIVE HEARINGS


INTERVENORS SUZANNE C. JAMES’ AND BRUCE L. JAMES’, INDIVIDUALLY AND AS REPRESENTATIVES OF REATA RIVER RANCH, LP’S 	RESPONSE TO ONCOR’S AND LCRA’S OBJECTION TO SECOND SUPPLEMENTAL DIRECT TESTIMONY OF MAY 23, 2026 FROM BRUCE L. JAMES

	
COME NOW, Suzanne C. James (S. James) and Bruce L. James (B. James), Individually (collectively the Jameses) and as Representatives of the Reata River Ranch, LP, (the Reata), Intervenors in the above entitled and numbered matter before the Public Utility Commission, and file this their Response to Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC’s (Oncor) and LCRA TSC’s (LCRA) (collectively Applicants) Objection (Item No, 5217) to Bruce L. James’ Second Supplemental Direct Testimony (Item No. 5101) filed on May 23, 2026, and request that Applicants’ Objection be overruled and request that the ALJ/Commission accept the supplemental direct testimony of May 23, 2026 from Intervenor B. James.  Alternatively, Intervenors S. James, B. James and the Reata respectfully requests the ALJ to grant leave to include his Second Supplemental Direct Testimony as evidence in this matter in light of the upcoming week long hearing on the Application of Oncor and LCRA to Amend their Application for a Certificate of Convenience and Necessity for a Proposed 765-kV Transmission Line from their Bell County East Switch to their Big Hill Substation.  In support of this Response, Intervenors S. James, B. James, and the Reata would respectfully show the following:
I.
	The purpose of a system of procedures is to “promote the just and efficient disposition of proceedings and public participation in the decision making process.”  PUC Proc. R. §22.1(a). (Emphasis added).  The PUC specifically declares that the Texas Rules of Evidence “…must be followed in contested cases.” PUC Proc. R. §22.221(a).  As stated in the Texas Rules of Evidence, in the Purpose section:  “These rules should be construed so as to administer every proceeding fairly, eliminate unjustifiable expense and delay, and promote the development of evidence law, to the end of ascertaining the truth and securing a just determination.”  Tex. R. Evid. 102. (Emphasis added).  Applicants’ objection to Intervenor B. James’ Second Supplemental Direct Evidence of May 23, 2026, in light of the circumstances explained below, is unjust, prevents Intervenor B. James complete participation in the proceeding as a member of the public, is unfair in light of the disproportionate resources available to Applicants’ legal squads, will not cause an unjustifiable delay, and will help prevent securing a just determination in this matter.
II.
 	Intervenor B. James has never been a party to, or participated in, or testified in a PUC hearing until this matter, which must be described as an expedited, compressed proceeding at best.  Intervenors S. James, B. James, and the Reata filed their Motion to Intervene (Item No. 378) on April 10, 2026, and were admitted as Intervening parties in SOAH Order No. 9 (Item No. 2904) on April 27, 2026.  On April 20, 2026, the administrative law judges (ALJs) from the State Office of Administrative Hearings (SOAH) filed SOAH Order No. 6, establishing a procedural schedule, including a deadline of May 13, 2026, for Intervenors to file Testimony or Statement of Position.  No mention is made in SOAH Order No. 6 of a prohibition to supplement any timely filed initial Direct Testimony by Intervenors.  Intervenors S. James, B. James, and the Reata represent themselves, are in their seventies, and are trying to protect their way of life as a long-time ranching family in their twilight years.
III.
On May 10, 2026, Intervenor S. James filed her Direct Testimony (Item No. 3749). No objections have been made by any other party to her Direct Testimony.
IV.
Intervenor B. James has made three (3) testimonial filings as follows:
(1)	On May 10, 2026, Intervenor B. James filed his initial Direct Testimony (Item No. 3751). No objections have been made by any other party to his May 10, 2026, Direct Testimony.
(2)	On May 11, 2026, Intervenor B. James filed his first Supplemental Direct Testimony (Item No. 3786). No objections have been made by any other party to his May 11, 2026, Supplemental Direct Testimony.
(3)	On May 23, 2026, Intervenor B. James filed his Second Supplemental Direct Testimony (Item No. 5101) to his previous Direct Testimony filings shown above, which contains only three (3) additional pages of testimony basically about transmission tower lighting under FAA  AC 70/7460-1M. Applicants now object to Intervenor B. James’ May 23, 2026, Second Supplemental Filing as being untimely under SOAH Order No. 6.  See Item No. 5217, Pages 2 and 5.  

V.
	Applicants’ objection to Intervenor B. James’ Second Supplemental Testimony of May 23, 2026, appears to only be one of timing as expressed in their Objection.  Applicants fail to show how Intervenor B. James’ three (3) page supplemental testimony is actually unduly prejudicial to them in their recent objection filing.  Intervenor B. James requests that Applicants’ objection be overruled in that “his testimony is necessary for a full disclosure of the facts and admission of the (supplemental) testimony would not be unduly prejudicial to the rights of any party.” PUC Proc. R. §22.225(a)(10). (Emphasis added).  Applicants have put in issue the request to build a monstrous 210+ mile, first of its kind, 765 kV transmission line from the I-35 corridor of the state to the Permian Basin.  Their application describes the transmission towers to be erected and the height of the same.  Certainly, the issue of hazardous lighting required to be installed on top of the hideous transmission towers is implicated and should be expected in cross-examination of Applicants’ witnesses.  Intervenor B. James’ May 23, 2026, Second Supplemental Testimony should be of no surprise to Oncor and the LCRA and their armies of attorneys at Jackson Walker and Vinson & Elkins. 
VI.
	It is impossible for the public members such as the Jameses to review and totally comprehend the mass/mountain of filings in this matter in the time allotted.  Oncor’s and LCRA’s Application and initial Direct Testimony of numerous witnesses exceed 2,000 pages alone.  There are now over 5,200 Items appearing on the Interchange for this matter.  The issue of transmission tower lighting only arose in Intervenor B. James’ mind after he read the submission of rebuttal testimony from Frederick B. Wulff, Jr’s Rebuttal Testimony on May 22, 2026 (Item No. 4983).   Intervenor B. James’ second supplemental direct testimony was filed a day later.  Applicants’ objection simply equates to a claim that Intervenor B. James has no right to offer re-direct testimony.
VII.
Intervenors S. James, B. James and the Reata respectfully request that the ALJ/Commission overrule Applicant’s objection as to his Second Supplemental Direct Testimony filing of May 23, 2026, and accept the supplemental direct testimony of May 23, 2026, from Intervenor B. James, despite its claimed late filing. Good cause for the delay exists, as the information contained in the testimony was only recently recognized and was inadvertently not included in the original submission due to the mass filings in this matter. Allowing this testimony will not unduly prejudice any party, and Intervenors are prepared to accommodate any reasonable requests for additional response time by Applicants. Acceptance of this filing will ensure a complete and accurate record, serving the interests of justice and of the public. Any supposed delay is minimal and will not disrupt the proceeding's schedule.
WHEREFORE, PREMISES CONSIDERED, Intervenors S, James, B. James, and the Reata respectfully request that the ALJ/Commission take Notice of their Response to Oncor’s and LCRA’s  Objection (Item No, 5217) to Bruce L. James’ Second Supplemental Direct Testimony (Item No. 5101) filed on May 23, 2026, and request that Applicants’ objection be overruled and request that the ALJ/Commission accept the supplemental direct testimony of May 23, 2026 from Intervenor B. James, or alternatively, grant leave to include his Second Supplemental Direct Testimony as evidence, and for such other and further relief to which Intervenors S, James, B. James, and the Reata are justly entitled.
						

Respectfully submitted,
						Suzanne C. James
						Bruce L. James
						Reata River Ranch, LP
						P.O. Box 567
						Brady, Texas 76825
						Telephone (210) 273-2425 
						Facsimile (817) 878-0501
